content.rule: First Conditional (If + Present Simple, Subject + will / can / may + infinitive)
content.explanation: We use the first conditional to talk about possible future situations and their probable results.
content.example: If it is hot tomorrow, I will make a smoothie.

items.notes: Transcribed from the source book; teacher verification required.

content.explanation: A phrasal verb combines a verb with a preposition to create a specific meaning, such as organizing or cleaning.
content.example: Can you help me tidy up my bedroom?

content.script:
Mom: Hi Mariam, how was your day?
Mariam: Oh, hi Mom! It was a strange day, actually. We had a power outage! My class and I were looking at the interactive whiteboard, when suddenly all the information disappeared.
Mom: Really? That is strange! What did Miss Amira do?
Mariam: Well, first she got an extension cable and tried a different power socket, but that wasn't working either.

items.notes: Transcribed from the source book; teacher verification required.

content.question: What happened while Mariam's class was looking at the interactive whiteboard?
content.reason: Mariam reports that a power outage caused all information on the whiteboard to disappear.
